title: Complexity of the Full MiMC Algebraic Attack
summary: General complexity estimation for the attack's solving steps is difficult; reliable estimates for the complete procedure remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: The unresolved problem is to obtain reliable complexity estimates for solving the multivariate polynomial systems arising from the generic algebraic attack on full MiMC. The relevant solution procedure computes a Gr?bner basis in degree-reverse-lexicographic order, converts it to lexicographic order, factorizes a univariate polynomial in the resulting basis, and back-substitutes its roots. General complexity estimation for these steps is difficult; the needed analysis should quantify the cost of the complete procedure, including Gr?bner-basis computation and subsequent solving, for generic systems with $N$ polynomials in $V$ variables over a base field $F$ and degree of regularity $D_{\mathrm{reg}}$.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of full MiMC using multivariate polynomial-system solving.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Obtain reliable complexity estimates for the complete solving procedure, including Gr?bner-basis computation and subsequent solving.

citations.label: An Algebraic Attack on Ciphers with Low-Degree Round Functions: Application to Full MiMC

progress.summary: The source describes the Gröbner-basis-based solving workflow and states that estimating the complexity of its steps is generally hard. It presents complexity estimation for the complete workflow as the unresolved problem.
